title: Watching alone wasn’t enough, so these Filipino YouTube fans found each other offline
summary: Discovering YouTube creators like Dan and Phil and Smosh was a solitary experience. Filipino fans are making it a communal one.

blocks.text: Alone in the glow of the computer screen — that’s how many who grew up watching YouTube started.

In 2005, when the platform was conceived, it was geared to be a dating website where people could upload videos “talking about the partner of their dreams.” More than two decades later, video reigns social media, and YouTube is the second-most-visited website in the world.

It’s hard to imagine that the first few YouTube creators knew they could make a career out of the website when it began. Many have since stepped away. But some, including Dan and Phil and the Smosh channel, were able to build fandoms that have stuck with them for well over a decade.
“When I first started watching them, I didn’t even have a concept of stanning people,” recalled Wayne Pontalba, an admin of Dan and Phil Manila, who got into the fandom in the early 2010s.

Even back then, Daniel Howell and Philip Lester went only by their nicknames, always in tandem: Dan and Phil. They were among the first famous YouTubers, rising right as the platform boomed, and viewers “shipping” them together fueled much of their popularity.
Wayne was one of these fans, and she found only one other comrade in her class. They became best friends.

“We were the two weirdest people in the classroom,” she said. They weren’t quiet about their interest in these British YouTubers, even mimicking their videos in a school talent segment while barely understanding the words.
Meanwhile, Reese Reyes, an admin of Smosh Philippines Fans, didn’t have her own computer at ten years old, so she’d march her way to her neighbor’s house to watch Smosh on YouTube.
“I was the only one addicted to YouTube,” she said. “Unsupervised, as a kid,” she added.
Back then, Ian and Anthony were just two loud teenagers posting lip-sync videos online, but they would go on to become YouTube’s most subscribed channel in their heyday.

Reese’s interest in them waxed and waned as the channel evolved, with companies buying the Smosh channel out, new faces being brought in, and one half of the duo, Anthony, leaving. She’d fall right back in when the original duo bought the company back and geared their content towards their new motto.

blocks.caption: A photo of Smosh’s current cast. Photo from Smosh’s Instagram page.

blocks.text: “Their motto is ‘comedy rooted in friendship,’ and I can see it as a viewer,” Reese remarked. “I’m thankful for YouTube because it gave me a little space of solace to fangirl.”
Now, with fan events happening left and right, that little space of solace no longer belongs to just the screen.
Live, in person
For Marj Castro of Dan and Phil Manila, the first event she organized was out of necessity.
“Dan and Phil skipped the Philippines in their 2024 tour, and I felt how sad the fanbase was about it,” she said.

She organized it all by herself. After an interest check drew 30 responses, she booked a cafe that could cater to that size, dolled up the place, and warmly greeted everyone who walked in. The event was a success, so much so that four more admins joined the team after it.
“It was a communal way to say [to Dan and Phil] that, ‘Hey, we’re still here!’” said James Mortilla, one of the new admins, about why he joined the planning of their latest event.
I was there for it on the afternoon of October 18. The Recto cafe’s brutalist interior was hidden well under purple nylon balloons and animated drawings of the internet couple.

blocks.caption: Participants find their seats as Dan and Phil Manila’s Howlter High cupsleeve event begins in Kape Light Recto, Sampaloc, Manila, on October 18, 2026. All photos by Aidan Bernales/Rappler.

blocks.text: Throughout the afternoon, attendees in bedazzled outfits came up to give away stickers of their Dan and Phil fan art. I asked one of them if the organizers had commissioned her. She said no: the stickers were free, she had printed them herself, and she brought enough for everyone in the room.
“It is such an honor to be a medium for fans to interact with each other in real life,” Wayne commented. “It’s not every day you see someone who watches the same YouTuber that you do.”

blocks.caption: A Howlter High attendee poses with standees of YouTubers Dan and Phil, illustrated by another Filipino fan.

blocks.text: Smosh Philippines Fans began the same way, with fans who couldn’t be where the creators were. It started as a Discord server, Bahay ni Ian, in 2025 with around 30 to 50 fans who’d found each other through other social media platforms. When Smosh held a live show, the server pooled donations toward a livestream ticket and streamed it for a watch party.
The server has since grown past 600 members and spilled out of the online sphere.
At an October 24 board game event in a cafe in España, I met a group of six friends who became close, thanks to Smosh Philippines Fans.

“Smosh’s motto is ‘comedy rooted in friendship,’ right? That’s also what happened to us,” said Hywel Jintalan, one of the attendees. The group barely fit on the small couch, so one of them sprawled across the others’ legs like a baby. They had “yearned for a friendship” like this: hanging out after school and work, playing the board games they’d only ever enjoyed vicariously through Smosh.

blocks.caption: Smosh fans prepare for a round of Blood on the Clocktower during Smosh Philippines Fans’ board game event at Coffee + Co, Sampaloc, Manila on October 24, 2026.

blocks.text: The games are a nod to Smosh Games, one of the channel’s most popular offshoots, which is devoted to games of all sorts. Tables were littered with board game pieces and players screaming in jest. In a conference room, players spoke in low voices and cast suspicious glances at each other over a roleplaying game. A Dress To Impress contest, a live reenactment of the Roblox fashion game, was held. The winning fit? A lifeguard costume with a floatie, a nod to a Smosh summer series.

blocks.caption: Smosh fans, dressed up as lifeguards, man the sign-ups for Last Splash of Blood.

blocks.text: Whether you’re extroverted or introverted, Kiki Langahid, Smosh Philippines Fans’ social media manager, says it doesn’t matter. “It doesn’t hinder anyone from playing games,” she remarked. “It’s people who love playing board games and having a good time with their friends.”
A special shoutout
The creators they gather for are entire continents away, but the internet does this funny thing where it closes the distance.
At another cupsleeve event last year, Dan and Phil surprised attendees with a video message.
“To all the Filipino fans, we appreciate you out there where it’s nice and warm,” Dan said, looking over at Phil for an extra comment. “Enjoy the meetup!” Phil exclaimed.

Surprise! Some familiar faces had a special message for us during the #TerriblyInPHluencedCSE 😁👋 Maraming salamat @danielhowell and @AmazingPhil for making our day extra special 💙#DNPMNLCSE2025 pic.twitter.com/uZmB3Z8ED8— Dan and Phil Manila (@DanAndPhilMNL) October 18, 2025
“It was one of the hardest secrets I had to keep,” Marj said. It was a complete shot in the dark when she sent that email to Dan and Phil’s manager; she couldn’t believe her eyes when they responded.

The pair’s manager stayed in contact with the team afterward, even sponsoring the merchandise giveaways for the next fan meet. Attendees who won the games the admins organized went home with signed photo cards.

blocks.caption: Dan and Phil fans pose with their signed photo cards after winning a game during Howlter High.

blocks.text: This December, Dan and Phil themselves are coming. They’re bringing their Hard Launch World Tour to Manila on December 4. It will be their first Philippine show since 2018.
Smosh hasn’t announced any plans yet to come here, but Kiki has made it her goal to bring them.

She recalls an event where attendees dressed as characters played by Smosh cast member Amanda Lehan-Canto, just as a Filipino producer of the show was visiting the country. They invited her, but she was out of town spending time with family.
Nevertheless, they persisted. Their flashiest effort yet is one you might have seen: an LED birthday greeting for Lehan-Canto that ran for a whole day in Guadalupe, EDSA.
She reacted to it on a Smosh podcast she co-hosts. “They had a bigger celebration for your birthday than you did!” fellow cast member Shayne Topp joked.
The people who get it
It’s easy for these events to be all about the creators. But really, it’s about the people there.
For Mikhail Valdez, the Smosh events are special. “It’s one of the few times I get to socialize,” he said.

He wouldn’t consider Smosh “niche” now, but when he started watching them, he couldn’t find anyone to talk about their videos with. Then he met two people who were also interested, and they became close.
“It became bigger and bigger to the point that I get to attend social events like these,” he said. Nearly 30 people filled that cafe in España. For Mikhail, it was a long way from two friends.

blocks.caption: Mikhail Valdez and fellow game participants pose with their role chips after completing a round of Blood on the Clocktower.

blocks.text: Noeri David and Cielo Fortin, who attended the Dan and Phil event, reconnected only recently.

“We stopped communicating because of our high school lives,” Noeri told me. “But when Dan and Phil hard launched last year, I reached out to [Cielo] again. I didn’t even anticipate that she’d reply back.”

All Noeri wanted was to tell Cielo she appreciated their time together, since Dan and Phil’s relationship had brought those memories back. Fortunately, Cielo replied, and their friendship picked up again.
“I’ve met so many people in this fandom that helped me survive,” Noeri said.

blocks.caption: Cielo Fortin and Noeri David, Dan and Phil fans, holding literal Dan and Phil fans.

blocks.text: Discovering these creators, whether two decades ago or just yesterday, was a solitary experience. But a singular decision to press play can bloom into a Saturday night of board games, sharing your art with strangers, and reigniting dormant friendships.

Joo Mondia, one of the Dan and Phil Manila admins, put it this way: “If there are those who don’t understand why you love these guys, there are over 200 people right now who will tell you otherwise.” — Rappler.com
Quotes translated to English for brevity.
